compatibility.metadata.title: Is Clear PVC Tubing Compatible with Cleaning Fluids? Clouding and IVD Validation
compatibility.metadata.seoTitle: PVC Tubing Chemical Compatibility: Cleaning Fluids & Clouding | FOREACH
compatibility.metadata.seoDescription: Evaluate PVC tubing chemical compatibility using 288-hour contact, 408-hour immersion and chemiluminescence background tests. Check appearance, dimensions, mass, hardness and device-level limits.
compatibility.metadata.coverAlt: FOREACH clear flexible PVC tubing, showing the tube wall and coiled form
compatibility.deck: Compatibility has two directions: can the cleaner change the tubing, and can tubing contact affect the assay? Cleaning-fluid exposure and background measurements help connect material screening with IVD device validation.
compatibility.leadBlocks.0.text: Whether clear PVC tubing, also called clear vinyl tubing, can carry an IVD cleaning fluid depends on the compound, cleaner formulation, working concentration, temperature and contact time. Whitening or clouding after immersion alone proves neither failure nor acceptance. Compare appearance before and after rinsing and drying, then check dimensions, mass, hardness, fluid background, assembled seals and flow.
compatibility.leadBlocks.1.text: In clinical chemistry and chemiluminescence analyzers, wash tubing is both a wetted material and part of the assay workflow. FOREACH E3602007 PVC tubing illustrates test methods and observations for specified cleaners, concentrations and exposure methods, helping engineers design their own validation.
compatibility.sections.0.title: Is PVC tubing resistant to cleaning fluids? What chemical compatibility testing must check
compatibility.sections.0.blocks.0.text: A cleaner can change tubing dimensions, hardness or surface condition, affecting barb fit and routing. The contacted liquid may also develop particles, discoloration or assay-background changes. These are different measurement targets; photographs after immersion cannot answer all of them.

compatibility.sections.0.blocks.3.text: A chemical compatibility chart is a screening tool. Sample testing must use the actual formulation and conditions. Raw-material biocompatibility documentation does not replace cleaner exposure testing or prove that finished tubing cannot affect a particular reagent or signal.
compatibility.sections.1.title: How do you test PVC tubing with cleaning fluids? Concentration, temperature and contact time
compatibility.sections.1.blocks.0.text: Two exposure methods were used: full immersion of the inner and outer surfaces, and filling the lumen. E3602007 was tested against TYGON ND-100-65 tubing. Cleaning fluid 1 and cleaning fluid 2 were each prepared with purified water as required. For each tubing material, each cleaner/exposure-method combination used 3 samples kept indoors in a cool, dry, ventilated location.
compatibility.sections.1.blocks.1.text: Conditions for the 288-hour cleaning-fluid contact test
compatibility.sections.1.blocks.2.rows.0: Short tubing sections fully submerged in prepared cleaner
compatibility.sections.1.blocks.2.rows.1: Cleaner filled into the tubing to observe internal-surface exposure
compatibility.sections.1.blocks.2.rows.2: Changed daily; test and reference groups used the same preparation batch
compatibility.sections.1.blocks.2.rows.3: After each 72-hour contact interval, specimens were removed, rinsed and air-dried for 24 hours as specified before measurement; results were recorded through 288 hours
compatibility.sections.1.blocks.2.rows.4: Appearance, liquid changes, ID, OD, mass and Shore A hardness
compatibility.sections.1.blocks.3.text: Daily fluid replacement and removal for measurement after each 72-hour contact interval are separate operations. Replacement renews the contact fluid; rinsing and 24 hours of air-drying define the specimen condition for weighing and dimensional checks. Weighing wet tubing against a dry baseline introduces adhering-liquid mass, so sample preparation must be recorded.
compatibility.sections.1.blocks.4.text: This test used ID/OD changes within ±0.15 mm, mass within ±10% of baseline and hardness within 65±5A as acceptance limits, alongside appearance and liquid checks. A new device needs limits based on its dimensional tolerances, fitting interface and assay requirements; these values are not universal IVD standards.
compatibility.sections.2.title: Can clear PVC tubing still be used after turning white? Appearance, mass and hardness checks
compatibility.sections.2.blocks.0.text: Distinguish whitening during contact from changes that remain after rinsing and drying. These samples recovered their original color without observed deformation or cracking. Suitability for a device still depends on wet-state clarity, dimensions, hardness, connections and assay criteria. Recovered clarity alone identifies neither the mechanism nor the complete validation outcome.
compatibility.sections.2.blocks.1.text: The following E3602007 mass changes were measured at 288 hours after rinsing and drying. Each range covers 3 samples; signs show the direction of change from initial mass.
compatibility.sections.2.blocks.4.text: E3602007 measured 70A both initially and after 288 hours in the full-immersion tests with both cleaners. Separate nominal hardness from an individual reading: 70A is at the upper limit of the 65±5A acceptance band and was unchanged in this measurement.
compatibility.sections.2.blocks.5.alt: PVC tubing ends, walls and surface appearance before cleaning-fluid exposure
compatibility.sections.2.blocks.5.captio: Initial tubing appearance provides the baseline for tube-end, wall and surface comparisons.
compatibility.sections.2.blocks.6.text: Both test and reference tubing showed surface whitening after immersion, before rinsing. Original color returned after rinsing with water and air-drying, with no observed deformation or cracks. Recovery after drying does not mean clarity stayed constant during contact. If bubbles must be seen through the wall, assess clarity while the tubing contains the actual fluid.
compatibility.sections.2.blocks.7.alt: PVC tubing ends, walls and surface appearance after 288 hours of cleaning-fluid contact
compatibility.sections.2.blocks.7.captio: Tubing appearance after the 288-hour test. Compare samples under consistent rinsing, drying and observation conditions.
compatibility.sections.2.blocks.8.text: Weighing measures net mass change. A small change alone does not prove zero leaching or no material migration. Those questions require suitable analytical methods, detection capability and evaluation criteria.
compatibility.sections.3.title: Can PVC tubing handle concentrated cleaner? Comparing 408-hour immersion with diluted cleaner
compatibility.sections.3.blocks.0.text: A separate test used customer-supplied clinical chemistry cleaner, both as supplied and diluted at 1:19, with E3602007 and reference tubing at ambient temperature and humidity. There were 4 groups. The planned procedure was removal, rinsing, drying, visual inspection and weighing every 3 days, followed by fresh cleaner and continued immersion.
compatibility.sections.3.blocks.1.text: The first contact interval was 48 hours; subsequent intervals were 72 hours, totaling 408 hours of fluid contact. Samples were removed and contact was paused during the schedule. Use cumulative contact time rather than describing the full calendar period as uninterrupted operation.
compatibility.sections.3.blocks.2.text: E3602007 endpoint measurements after 408 cumulative hours of immersion
compatibility.sections.3.blocks.4.text: These endpoints show small net mass changes for the specific samples, exposure and weighing method. Sample numbers and conditions were limited; the result cannot be generalized to every PVC compound, cleaner concentration or long-term dynamic duty.
compatibility.sections.4.title: Can PVC tubing affect chemiluminescence background? Testing against a cleaner blank
compatibility.sections.4.blocks.0.text: Exposure testing evaluates observable tubing changes; background testing also examines the contacted liquid. Each of two cleaners was tested as unexposed reference liquid, liquid contacted with FOREACH tubing and liquid contacted with reference tubing. Approximately 300 μL was measured daily on the same chemiluminescence analyzer platform.
compatibility.sections.4.blocks.1.text: The plan covered 14 days. The analyzer-supplied cleaner produced 11 days of valid data, and the customer cleaner produced 14 days. The table gives each group's minimum and maximum valid readings to describe background variation on that platform.
compatibility.sections.4.blocks.2.text: Ranges of recorded luminescence-background readings across valid measurements
compatibility.sections.4.blocks.4.text: The reference liquid also varies, so a single day's difference cannot automatically be attributed to tubing. No directional background trend was observed in the tubing-contact groups under these conditions. The ranges are descriptive, not proof of no interference in every assay, and do not replace sample testing, carryover assessment or device wash-performance validation.
compatibility.sections.5.title: How do you validate an IVD wash line? From tubing compatibility to the installed device
compatibility.sections.5.blocks.0.text: Proceed from fluid contact to the connection assembly and then the assay workflow. Screen candidate tubing with the actual cleaner, pair exposed tubing with the intended fittings, and check washing, draining, idle periods and repeated operation in the device. This connects material observations with actual failure modes.
Define the cleaner: name or safety data sheet, working concentration, preparation water, maximum temperature, longest idle contact and replacement procedure. List concentrate and working solution separately.
Define the tubing: full part number, ID × OD, hardness, length and lot. Keep unexposed specimens as controls.
Check connections: use the actual barbed fitting and insertion depth to retest sealing, pull-off force, flow and pressure, including device routing and tensile loads.
Check the assay workflow: retain an unexposed-cleaner blank, define background and other relevant endpoints, and record repeatability and acceptance methods.
compatibility.sections.5.blocks.2.text: FOREACH can review PVC tubing and connection requirements for a project. The E3602007 values here are results from specified samples. FEP or other materials need their own dimensional, end-connection and actual-cleaner exposure assessment; PVC findings do not transfer automatically.
PVC tubing pressure tests, burst pressure and fitting pull-off force
Medical PVC tubing: dimensional control, manufacturing and traceability
FEP tubing properties and instrument connections
compatibility.sections.6.title: When should compatibility be revalidated after changing the cleaner or PVC tubing?
compatibility.sections.6.blocks.0.text: Changing cleaner brand, formulation, concentration, preparation water, maximum temperature, longest idle contact or replacement frequency can change exposure outcomes. Even with E3602007, check whether the new conditions fall within validated coverage before choosing additional tests. Results for cleaning fluids 1 and 2 apply only to the respective tested fluids.
compatibility.sections.6.blocks.1.text: After changes to tubing formulation, dimensions, fittings or the wash process, reassess material contact, sealing and assay performance according to the change. Keep before-and-after samples and cleaner blanks, using consistent preparation and acceptance methods to compare device relevance.
compatibility.cta.title: Review tubing and connections for your actual cleaning fluid
compatibility.cta.description: Provide cleaner and concentration, temperature, contact cycle, tubing dimensions, fittings and assay endpoints to define candidate materials and sample-validation scope.
pressure.metadata.title: Why Does Tubing Pull Off Barbed Fittings? PVC Pressure and Pull-Off Tests
pressure.metadata.seoTitle: Barbed Fitting Pull-Off: PVC Tubing Pressure & Burst Tests | FOREACH
pressure.metadata.seoDescription: Compare pressure-hold, burst, working-pressure and pull-off results for two PVC tubing sizes, including aging at 70°C for 42 days. Review fitting combinations and limits for IVD validation.
pressure.metadata.coverAlt: Close-up photograph of clear PVC tubing connected to a barbed fitting
pressure.deck: A fitting can release before the PVC tube bursts, and high pull-off force does not directly establish working pressure. FOREACH tests on two tubing sizes show how to measure and interpret pressure and post-aging retention before validating the installed IVD fluid path.
pressure.leadBlocks.0.text: Investigate tubing-to-barb dimensions, assembly condition, operating pressure and external tension when tubing pulls off a barbed fitting. An intact tube does not prove connection retention; a high initial pull-off force may change after temperature or fluid exposure. Validate connection pressure-hold, tube burst and fitting pull-off separately before defining an IVD assembly's operating range.
pressure.leadBlocks.1.text: The tubing discussed has approximate ID × OD dimensions of 1.6×3.2 mm and 3.2×6.4 mm. Table averages are test results for specified samples and fittings, useful for selection and validation methods; they are not rated working pressures for an entire series or arbitrary connections.
pressure.sections.0.title: Why does tubing pull off a barbed fitting? Fit, pressure peaks and external tension
pressure.sections.0.blocks.0.text: Barbed tube fittings retain tubing through deformation and contact around the barb. ID, wall thickness, hardness and barb profile determine fit; insufficient insertion, damaged ends or sideways loading can change retention. First establish whether release follows assembly, pump/valve switching or maintenance movement, then select the checks.
pressure.sections.0.blocks.2.rows.0.1: Actual ID, barb dimensions, hardness, insertion depth and tube-end condition
pressure.sections.0.blocks.2.rows.0.2: Pull-off and leak tests on the final assembly

pressure.sections.0.blocks.2.rows.1.1: Pressure peaks, blockage and supplementary restraint
pressure.sections.0.blocks.2.rows.1.2: Assembly pressure-hold and actual pressure cycling
pressure.sections.0.blocks.2.rows.2.0: Connection changes after fluid contact or heating
pressure.sections.0.blocks.2.rows.2.1: Fluid, temperature, tubing dimensions and hardness changes
pressure.sections.0.blocks.2.rows.2.2: Pressure-hold, sealing and pull-off after exposure
pressure.sections.0.blocks.2.rows.3.1: Bends, slack, supports and external tension
pressure.sections.0.blocks.2.rows.3.2: Reproduce actual routing and maintenance loads
pressure.sections.0.blocks.3.text: Adding a clamp is not a universal remedy. Confirm supplementary restraint against tubing, fitting and space requirements, then validate the final arrangement. Separating connection pressure-hold, tube burst and axial pull-off avoids using one pressure number to explain every release.
pressure.sections.1.title: PVC tubing working pressure, pressure-hold, burst pressure and pull-off force: what differs?
pressure.sections.1.blocks.0.rows.0.1: Specified tubing-and-fitting combination; units such as MPa
pressure.sections.1.blocks.0.rows.0.2: Whether it releases or reaches another defined failure within a specified pressure/time condition
pressure.sections.1.blocks.0.rows.1.2: When that specimen fails under the test conditions
pressure.sections.1.blocks.0.rows.2.1: Axial force separating tubing from a fitting, in N
pressure.sections.1.blocks.0.rows.2.2: Resistance of the specified assembly to axial tension
pressure.sections.1.blocks.0.rows.3.1: Product or assembly under defined fluid, temperature and use conditions
pressure.sections.1.blocks.0.rows.3.2: Permissible design operating range supported by specifications and validation
pressure.sections.1.blocks.1.text: Internal pressure, tubing deformation and fitting engagement interact in a barb connection. If the connection releases first, the tube may not reach its burst condition. Extra restraint used to reach tube burst also changes the assembly. Always evaluate the failure location and installation method alongside the result.
pressure.sections.1.blocks.2.text: Device design must include pressure peaks from pump start/stop, valve switching and blockage. A single ambient-temperature average does not replace temperature, cleaner-exposure, pressure-cycling or lot-variation validation. Dividing it by an arbitrary fixed factor does not establish a rating.
pressure.sections.2.title: How are PVC tubing pressure-hold and burst tested? Why barb restraint matters
pressure.sections.2.blocks.0.text: A manual hydrostatic tester applied increasing pressure at ambient temperature and humidity. The plan specified 5 specimens per size, about 300 mm long. Tubing with 1.6 mm ID used BA-16F-PP-N barbs; tubing with 3.2 mm ID used BA-32F-PP-N barbs. The key difference was whether extra restraint could be added at the connection.
pressure.sections.2.blocks.1.text: Differences between connection pressure-hold and tube burst testing
pressure.sections.2.blocks.2.rows.0.1: No supplementary fastener at the barb interface; record pressure held for more than 60 seconds without pull-off
pressure.sections.2.blocks.2.rows.1.1: Supplementary connection restraint permitted to prevent early pull-off; continue pressurization and record tube burst pressure
pressure.sections.2.blocks.2.rows.2.1: Keep individual readings and averages. Some sizes have fewer than 5 valid burst readings; planned sample count is not the valid count for every test
pressure.sections.2.blocks.3.text: This separates retention from tube-wall strength. Quoting a higher burst result without the extra-restraint condition could suggest that an unrestrained barb holds the same pressure. Validate the complete assembly intended for delivery.
pressure.sections.3.title: How much pressure can PVC tubing withstand? Hydrostatic results for two sizes
pressure.sections.3.blocks.0.text: The table summarizes ambient-temperature hydrostatic averages. Dimensions are ID × OD in mm; pressure is in MPa. E36 and M36 identify FOREACH 65A and 55A tubing respectively; TYGON ND-100-65 is the specified commercial reference. Comparisons concern that grade, not other products or price categories.
pressure.sections.3.blocks.1.text: Ambient-temperature hydrostatic averages for specified tubing/fitting combinations
pressure.sections.3.blocks.2.headers.2: Mean pressure held for 60 seconds without pull-off
pressure.sections.3.blocks.3.text: For E3602007 at 3.2×6.4 mm, mean connection pressure-hold was 1.48 MPa and mean tube burst was 2.62 MPa. Different connection restraint was used; the latter is not the unrestrained connection's capability. A useful pressure inquiry must include size, fitting, installation method, temperature and fluid.
pressure.sections.3.blocks.4.text: The table compares these samples under specified conditions but cannot attribute all differences to hardness. Compound, measured dimensions and barb fit also contribute. Recheck new barb profiles or sizes even when nominal ID is unchanged.
pressure.sections.4.title: Does aging affect PVC tubing pull-off force? A 70°C, 42-day test
pressure.sections.4.blocks.0.text: Pull-off testing used a different fitting set: SB-U28-16-PP-N for the smaller tubing and SB-U28-32-PP-N for the larger. After initial measurements, tubing was aged in a 70°C chamber, removed weekly, fitted to the appropriate barb and measured on a tensile tester through day 42. No supplementary fastener was used.
pressure.sections.4.blocks.1.text: This measures tubing assembled after thermal aging. It is not aging of a continuously assembled, pressurized connection exposed to cleaner. Device working pressure and service life need device-specific validation; a 70°C, 42-day test alone cannot establish a year's operating life.
pressure.sections.4.blocks.2.text: Pull-off results for tubing assembled after aging at 70°C
pressure.sections.4.blocks.4.expression: Decrease = (initial mean − day 42 mean) ÷ initial mean × 100%
pressure.sections.4.blocks.4.note: Calculated from the rounded means in the table; descriptive comparison, not a service-life decay model.
pressure.sections.4.blocks.5.alt: Mean pull-off force from day 0 to 42 for 1.6×3.2 mm PVC tubing: ND-100-65, M3602002 and E3602002
pressure.sections.4.blocks.5.caption: Pull-off force for 1.6×3.2 mm tubing (ID × OD). Horizontal axis: aging time at 70°C, days; vertical axis: mean pull-off force, N. Tubing was removed after aging and then assembled for measurement.
pressure.sections.4.blocks.6.text: Intermediate points also matter. E3602002 averaged 31.3 N on day 7, below its day 42 value of 34.6 N. The smaller reference tubing averaged 11.0 N on day 7 and 16.0 N on day 42. Endpoints alone miss lower intermediate values. Review the full interval, individual variation and actual tensile loads when defining acceptance.
pressure.sections.4.blocks.7.alt: Mean pull-off force from day 0 to 42 for 3.2×6.4 mm PVC tubing: ND-100-65, M3602007 and E3602007
pressure.sections.4.blocks.7.caption: Pull-off force for 3.2×6.4 mm tubing (ID × OD). Horizontal axis: aging time at 70°C, days; vertical axis: mean pull-off force, N. Points represent initial and weekly measurements.
pressure.sections.5.title: Can barbed fitting pull-off force be converted into pressure? Axial load versus fluid pressure
pressure.sections.5.blocks.0.text: Pressure and force have different units and loading methods. F = P × A can estimate axial force on an effective area in an ideal case. Real barb connections also involve tube expansion, contact distribution, bending, friction and assembly variation; effective area cannot automatically be taken from a nominal dimension. This calculation supports load analysis, not a replacement for hydrostatic assembly testing.
pressure.sections.5.blocks.1.text: Passing a tube-burst test does not replace pull-off testing either. Assembly, lid opening, harness movement and consumable replacement can impose tension, even in a low-pressure line. Provide slack, support and sensible bend positions so the joint does not continually carry movement or maintenance loads.
pressure.sections.5.blocks.2.text: The hydrostatic and pull-off tests here used different barb models. Their tables cannot be combined into a complete specification for one assembly. Align the final tubing, fitting and installation requirements in a single validation plan.
pressure.sections.6.title: How can IVD tubing pull-off be prevented? Validating the barb assembly and installed line
pressure.sections.6.blocks.0.text: During development, screen material and connection samples, then test the actual assembly under the most demanding intended conditions. The sequence below helps separate material, fit, pressure and external-load issues and obtain comparable supplier samples.
pressure.sections.6.blocks.1.items.0: Fix the combination: tubing part number, ID/OD, tolerances, hardness, full fitting model, insertion depth, supplementary restraint and preassembly treatment.
pressure.sections.6.blocks.1.items.1: Record pressure conditions: normal operation, start/stop, valve switching and expected blockage; define peaks and cycles for validation.
pressure.sections.6.blocks.1.items.2: Include actual fluid and temperature: expose assemblies to the cleaner concentration, maximum temperature and idle cycle, then check sealing, pressure-hold and pull-off.
pressure.sections.6.blocks.1.items.3: Reproduce routing: bends, length, support points and maintenance tension; record whether failure is leakage, release or tube rupture.
pressure.sections.6.blocks.1.items.4: Define assembly acceptance: preserve individual results, sample count, lots and decision criteria before establishing the device's operating range.
pressure.sections.6.blocks.2.text: FOREACH PVC tubing and barbed fittings can be evaluated as a matched combination. These tests explain methods and results for specified combinations. Revalidate the final delivered assembly after changing tubing, size, fitting or restraint. Product cards provide specifications, not project-specific assembly-validation evidence.

pressure.sections.7.title: What should be retested after changing PVC tubing or barbed fittings?
pressure.sections.7.blocks.0.text: The same nominal ID does not ensure identical fit across tubing and fittings. After changing compound, hardness, tolerances, barb profile, insertion depth or restraint, recheck assembly, sealing, pressure-hold and pull-off on the new final combination.
pressure.sections.7.blocks.1.text: When introducing the assembly into production, include the validated tubing, fitting, assembly method and operating conditions in the acceptance requirements. Preserve individual results and lot information. Reassess changes against the same combination rather than carrying forward one old tubing-pressure number.
